key_insight: An AI teammate does more than help with decisions—it changes how human teammates talk to each other. The study shows that adding an artificial teammate reshapes communication patterns, revealing a social cost that matters in team settings.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the gap in understanding how conversational AI affects human-human communication inside small teams, especially during high-stakes collaborative decision-making.
method: Randomized controlled study comparing 16 mixed teams (2 students + 1 AI teammate) with 17 all-human teams.
Teams completed a high-stakes moral-dilemma decision task to elicit natural team discussion and coordination.
Used Group Communication Analysis (GCA), team surveys, and lexical analysis of team discourse to measure sociocognitive communication dynamics.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the key takeaway is that adding AI to a team can alter interpersonal communication, not just task performance. Designers of collaborative AI should evaluate social dynamics, communication quality, and trust—not only accuracy or efficiency.
visual_elements: Side-by-side team setup diagram: all-human vs human+AI teammate.
Workflow chart showing task -> discussion -> decision -> analysis metrics.
Communication network graphic illustrating changes in turn-taking or interaction patterns.
Simple bar/line charts comparing survey scores and discourse features across conditions.
paper_title: The Social Cost of an AI Teammate: How an Artificial Teammate Reshapes Human-Human Communication in Small-Team Decision-Making
paper_authors: Nia Nixon, Jaeyoon Choi, Pedro Martins De Bastos, Mohammad Amin Samadi, Luise Mehner
